government.title: When Do Citizens Support Corrupt Politicians? The Trade‐Offs Between Corruption and Competence
government.short_title: When Do Citizens Support Corrupt Politicians? The Trade‐Offs Between Corruption and Competence
government.plain_summary: This research explores why people still support corrupt politicians despite their dislike of corruption in general. It found that when mayoral candidates perform well economically, it helps reduce the negative impact of corruption on public support for those leaders. However, even with competent leadership, citizens value honesty more than competence. Additionally, people who live in areas with less corruption and have lower incomes are less likely to accept corrupt politicians as long as they're competent.

government.title: Do Performance Budgeting Reforms Reduce Corruption? Evidence From a Quasi‐Experimental Study
government.short_title: Do Performance Budgeting Reforms Reduce Corruption? Evidence From a Quasi‐Experimental Study
government.plain_summary: This research looks at whether changing how governments allocate their budgets based on performance results helps reduce corruption. It found that when local Chinese governments started using this new method, they had fewer actual cases of corruption and people thought there was less of it happening too. The study suggests these changes made government spending more transparent and efficient, which helped keep officials from doing things they shouldn't. This research shows how changing the way money is managed can make a difference in preventing bad behavior by those who work for governments.

government.title: Blame Avoidance and Corruption: How Politicians' Denials Shape Citizen Perceptions and Political Accountability
government.short_title: Blame Avoidance and Corruption: How Politicians' Denials Shape Citizen Perceptions and Politic…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how politicians accused of corruption respond when they deny their wrongdoing. The research shows that when politicians say they are innocent or blame others for their actions, it can improve their image and chances of winning elections. This is especially true for people who strongly support one political party. Understanding this helps us see how leaders influence public opinion about corruption in politics.

government.title: Customer Experiences with Airline Refunds: An Analysis of Procedures, Challenges, and Policy Implications
government.short_title: Customer Experiences with Airline Refunds: An Analysis of Procedures, Challenges, and Policy I…
government.source: International Journal of Research in Entrepreneurship & Business Studies
government.plain_summary: This study analyzed how airlines handle airfare refunds and the challenges customers face during this process. It found that communication issues are a major problem, especially in understanding airline rules. Despite most customers being satisfied with their refund after receiving one, they felt the process was complex and inefficient. The research suggests clearer policies and better coordination between airlines, intermediaries, and customers could improve trust and service quality.

government.title: Strengthening Coastal Resilience through Science-Based Mangrove Governance in Davao Occidental, Philippines
government.short_title: Strengthening Coastal Resilience through Science-Based Mangrove Governance in Davao Occidental…
government.plain_summary: This research highlights that while investing in mangrove restoration in Davao Occidental has been significant, outcomes have varied widely due to issues like incorrect species selection and lack of monitoring. Studies show that by matching the right species to each site and diversifying plant types, survival rates can be very high at over 95%. However, these effective methods are not consistently used because there's no unified policy framework. The study suggests creating a standardized governance system that mandates correct species use, promotes diverse planting strategies, and establishes community monitoring systems supported by partnerships between local governments and universities.

government.title: Machine Learning for Job Matching, Skills Mapping and Labour Market Forecasting in e-Government Systems
government.short_title: Machine Learning for Job Matching, Skills Mapping and Labour Market Forecasting in e-Governmen…
government.source: Journal of Applied Science, Information and Computing
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how advanced machine learning techniques could improve job matching and forecasting in e-government systems used by the Tanzanian government. The main challenges identified were poor usability of the system, weak job skill matching, and lack of real-time updates. Machine learning models helped analyze data better for these issues. The research found that integrating ML into these systems can significantly enhance decision-making, increase efficiency, and match workers with available jobs more accurately.

government.title: Review of Risk Based Financial Governance Literature Shaping Institutional Investment Decision Practices
government.short_title: Review of Risk Based Financial Governance Literature Shaping Institutional Investment Decision…
government.plain_summary: Risk-based financial governance is becoming crucial for how institutions make investment decisions in today's markets. It involves assessing risks explicitly within oversight to align with organizational goals and responsibilities. This approach extends beyond traditional compliance by integrating risk into decision-making processes, using tools like scenario analysis and dynamic portfolio management. The literature shows that institutions with strong risk-based governance are better at anticipating market changes, optimizing performance, and ensuring sustainable value creation while staying compliant.

government.title: The Impact of Digital Technology on International Humanitarian Law: Ethical and Legal Implications of Autonomous Weapons Systems
government.short_title: The Impact of Digital Technology on International Humanitarian Law: Ethical and Legal Implicat…
government.source: European Journal of Law and Political Science
government.plain_summary: This article looks at how new technology like AI is changing international laws for wars. As weapons get more automated, it raises questions about who should be held responsible when they make decisions. The main idea is that current rules are still useful but need updating to fit with these new types of weapons. It suggests ways to improve the existing laws so that people in war zones can continue to rely on protections like not harming civilians unnecessarily.

government.title: The Transparency Paradox: How Digital Accountability Can Inflate Public Costs in Low-Trust Environments
government.short_title: The Transparency Paradox: How Digital Accountability Can Inflate Public Costs in Low-Trust Env…

government.title: Governance, Democracy & Psychological Wellbeing Psychology of a Corruption
government.short_title: Governance, Democracy & Psychological Wellbeing Psychology of a Corruption
government.source: Journal of Business and Econometrics Studies
government.plain_summary: This paper looks at corruption in Africa by examining how it affects governance, democracy, and mental health. It suggests that corruption is not just a legal issue but also stems from deep social and moral problems left over from colonial times. The study proposes solutions like strengthening institutions, developing ethical leaders, empowering citizens, and using restorative justice methods. By doing this, they aim to improve people's well-being and strengthen democratic systems in Africa.

government.title: Digital Governance and Anti-Corruption Transformation in Algeria: Evaluating the Role of Fiscal Digitization and E-Procurement Systems in Enhancing Administrative Transparency and Public Sector Integrity
government.short_title: Digital Governance and Anti-Corruption Transformation in Algeria: Evaluating the Role of Fisca…
government.source: Science, Education and Innovations in the context of modern problems
government.plain_summary: Digital governance in Algeria has been adopted as a strategy to combat corruption, especially in sectors like taxation and procurement. The country is digitizing tax administration and implementing electronic public procurement systems, which have improved transparency and accountability. These digital tools help reduce discretionary practices, enhance traceability, and improve access to information for the public. However, there are still challenges such as incomplete integration of digital systems, cybersecurity issues, and uneven administrative capacity that need addressing.

government.title: Lebanon
government.short_title: Lebanon
government.plain_summary: The IMF's diagnostic for Lebanon found widespread corruption issues across key government functions like fiscal management, banking supervision, and central bank operations. These problems are worsened by outdated laws, weak institutions, and a fragile legal system. This report suggests reforms focusing on strengthening the rule of law, improving financial sector oversight, and public finance management to boost economic recovery and ensure fair growth for all Lebanese people.

government.title: Corruption, Governance and the Challenges of the Rule of Law - Law Enforcement and Corruption - An Assessment of the Functioning of the Albanian State Police.
government.short_title: Corruption, Governance and the Challenges of the Rule of Law - Law Enforcement and Corruption…
government.plain_summary: Corruption has been a major issue in Albania for over three decades since its transition to democracy. This corruption spread within national security institutions like the State Police, leading to instability and even threatening their collapse. Efforts by governments have aimed at restructuring and purging corrupt elements from the police force, but political interference continues to be problematic. This undermines law enforcement effectiveness and the credibility of the police force, which is crucial for maintaining a functioning rule of law in Albania.

government.title: Alcohol and cancer risk: A review of messaging content on websites of medical, cancer, government, and nonprofit organizations and alcohol companies.
government.short_title: Alcohol and cancer risk: A review of messaging content on websites of medical, cancer, governm…
government.plain_summary: This study looked at websites from various organizations in the United States related to health, cancer, government, and nonprofits, as well as those funded by alcohol companies. Out of 126 medical society websites reviewed, about half mentioned health risks from alcohol use, with around a quarter mentioning cancer risk. Only six out of these societies stated there is no safe level of alcohol consumption. All governmental sites included both health and cancer risks related to alcohol.

government.title: AI Regulation and Its Social Impacts on Public Policy
government.short_title: AI Regulation and Its Social Impacts on Public Policy
government.plain_summary: AI is now a key part of how governments make decisions in many areas like healthcare, policing, and welfare. As more AI systems are used, it's important to have rules to make sure they work fairly and don't cause problems. These rules help ensure that AI doesn't lead to unfair treatment or less democracy. By carefully watching how AI is used, we can make sure it helps people and doesn't hurt them.

government.title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bilan d’une recherche immersive en Police Judiciaire française
government.short_title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bi…
government.plain_summary: This research focuses on understanding the emotional risks in police work and how they manage their emotions to improve job satisfaction. It was conducted by observing various police units like forensic science, digital investigation, financial division, criminal division, anti-terrorism unit, and more over 26 days. The study found two key emotions that are hard for them to express: interest and frustration. These emotions make it difficult for officers to discuss their work-related feelings openly, leading to invisible or undiscussed labor.

government.title: Data Science as a Catalyst for Audit Transformation
government.short_title: Data Science as a Catalyst for Audit Transformation
government.plain_summary: Data science has become crucial as we generate vast amounts of information daily. It helps transform this data into useful insights for better decision-making across various sectors. For audit institutions, integrating data science can enhance their ability to manage public funds more effectively and improve accountability. By using data science, audits can provide clearer and more accurate reports that recommend improvements faster, which benefits the overall administration and improves citizens' quality of life.

government.title: Killer Robots – A Case for SAIs
government.short_title: Killer Robots – A Case for SAIs
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses a scenario where autonomous killer robots are used in warfare without human intervention. These robots can make decisions about who to target based on AI algorithms trained to recognize certain uniforms. If one of these drones targets and kills an enemy soldier who is surrendering, it would violate international laws. Another concern is if the robot makes a mistake by attacking another similar system, leading to unintended conflicts.

government.title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the Lebanese case
government.short_title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the L…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to noble cause corruption in Lebanon, where there's a lot of social and economic hardship. The research found that feelings like compassion and selflessness often push people into doing good deeds for noble causes, but these actions sometimes involve corrupt practices. This leads to internal conflicts as the person feels both guilty and supported by their work environment. Factors like physical exchanges, personal space in the workplace, and close relationships with users can make it easier for this type of corruption to happen.

government.title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause noble à partir du cas libanais
government.short_title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause no…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to corruption for a noble cause in Lebanon, where corruption is prevalent and social issues are challenging. Based on interviews with 32 Lebanese public servants, the research explores how feelings of compassion and self-sacrifice related to public service motivation might encourage them to engage in corrupt behavior for what they see as a good cause. The study highlights that these motivations can lead to behaviors like providing extra support or shielding users from punishment. This can create internal conflicts within the public servant due to their emotional connection with those affected.

government.title: Optimization of the Implementation of Anti-SLAPP Measures in Safeguarding Freedom of Expression in Indonesia
government.short_title: Optimization of the Implementation of Anti-SLAPP Measures in Safeguarding Freedom of Expressio…
government.source: International Journal of Social Science and Human Research
government.plain_summary: This study examines how Indonesia uses anti-SLAPP measures to protect freedom of expression. During a period when democracy was declining, there were many protests that led to some activists facing unfair lawsuits. The law allows for misuse which can criminalize online activities. To fix this, the study suggests creating an Anti-SLAPP system using AI technology.

government.title: Research integrity and data ethics in AI-driven integrated healthcare: a critical appraisal
government.short_title: Research integrity and data ethics in AI-driven integrated healthcare: a critical appraisal
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how artificial intelligence is being used in healthcare and raises important questions about keeping studies honest and protecting patient data. It found that when using AI to make health decisions, it's hard to see exactly how these systems work, which can be a problem if patients need to understand their care. There are also concerns about whether the AI might unfairly favor certain groups based on past healthcare patterns. The study suggests creating a system where both experts in technology and those who use patient data work together to make sure everything is done ethically and transparently.

government.title: ARCHITECTURE OF ANTI-CORRUPTION POLICY INSTRUMENTS IN THE PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION SYSTEM
government.short_title: ARCHITECTURE OF ANTI-CORRUPTION POLICY INSTRUMENTS IN THE PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION SYSTEM
government.source: "EСONOMY FINANСES MANAGEMENT Topical issues of science and practical activity"
government.plain_summary: This article discusses how different tools and systems can work together in a structured way within government to prevent and fight against corruption. It emphasizes that these tools need to be connected at various levels of management for them to be most effective. Key tools like electronic declarations, open state registers, and anti-corruption programs are highlighted as important for increasing transparency and reducing risks of corruption. The article also points out common challenges in using these tools effectively.

government.title: The Master’s Tools—Anti-Bullying and Harassment Policy in Higher Education Institutions
government.short_title: The Master’s Tools—Anti-Bullying and Harassment Policy in Higher Education Institutions
government.source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
government.plain_summary: In higher education institutions, there's often a problem with how anti-bullying and harassment policies are written. These documents can make it seem like reporting issues is not really an option or that they're just for show. This makes it harder for people who have been bullied to speak up because the system might trick them into staying quiet. The result is that these institutions keep things as they are, which doesn't help prevent bullying and harassment from happening in the first place.

government.title: How Settler Colonialism, Capitalist Restructuring, Penal Reform and Anti-Prison Organizing are Shaping Prison Expansion in Eastern Ontario
government.short_title: How Settler Colonialism, Capitalist Restructuring, Penal Reform and Anti-Prison Organizing are…
government.plain_summary: The government in Ontario is planning to build a new prison called the Eastern Ontario Correctional Complex, which will have 235 beds. This decision comes from various forces like settler colonialism, capitalist restructuring, penal reform, and anti-prison organizing. These groups are working together to oppose building more prisons because they believe it perpetuates social marginalization. Understanding these influences helps in creating effective strategies against prison expansion.

government.title: Between INTOSAI and society's expectations: standard setting and the audit expectations gap in anti-corruption oversight
government.short_title: Between INTOSAI and society's expectations: standard setting and the audit expectations gap in…
government.source: Journal of Public Budgeting, Accounting & Financial Management
government.plain_summary: This study examines how international standards for fighting corruption, set by organizations like INTOSAI, sometimes don't align with what society expects from audits. The research found that when setting these standards, there was too much focus on prevention rather than detection of corruption. This led to a gap between the expectations people have and what the standards allow auditors to check. Practically speaking, this means public sector auditors might not be able to find all instances of corruption if they're only looking at preventive measures.

government.title: A path analysis on the effect of human development index, financial performance, and macroeconomic factors on local government financial accountability and transparency in Indonesia
government.short_title: A path analysis on the effect of human development index, financial performance, and macroecon…
government.source: International Journal of Management and Sustainability
government.plain_summary: This study examines how human development index (HDI), financial performance indicators like Regional Original Revenue (PAD) and General Allocation Fund (DAU), along with macroeconomic factors such as inflation and Gross Regional Domestic Product (GRDP), affect local government financial accountability and transparency in Indonesia. It found that HDI and DAU improve accountability directly and indirectly through transparency. PAD also contributes to transparency but not accountability. Inflation and GRDP had no significant effect on transparency, but they did have a slight impact on accountability.

government.title: Reforming the white coat economy: judicial evidence and institutional implications from China’s healthcare anti-corruption campaign
government.short_title: Reforming the white coat economy: judicial evidence and institutional implications from China’…
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how doctors and hospitals deal with money-related problems in China's healthcare system through court cases. They found that most issues came from doctors getting bribes for medicines or services, stealing hospital funds, or tricking insurance systems. The main places where these things happen are when buying medicine/supplies, checking if patients used their insurance correctly, and managing the money inside hospitals. When someone is caught doing wrong in court, they often get punished with time in jail, being watched by a judge instead of going to prison, or having to give back what was stolen.

government.title: Crisis of Public Trust in Government and the Challenges of Political Ethics in Contemporary Indonesia
government.short_title: Crisis of Public Trust in Government and the Challenges of Political Ethics in Contemporary In…
government.source: Journal of Islamic Law and Humanitarian Studies
government.plain_summary: In recent years, many people in Indonesia have lost faith in their government due to issues like corruption and inconsistent law enforcement. This loss of trust affects how they view the legitimacy of state institutions and politicians. To address this, it's important for leaders to act with higher ethical standards, be more transparent, and prioritize public welfare over personal or political interests. By doing so, they can help rebuild people’s confidence in their government and support a healthier democracy.

government.title: Towards Inclusive Excellence: Building an Anti-racist, Equity-oriented Community of Practice for STEM Faculty
government.short_title: Towards Inclusive Excellence: Building an Anti-racist, Equity-oriented Community of Practice f…
government.source: To Improve the Academy: A Journal of Educational Development
government.plain_summary: This study describes an initiative aimed at helping STEM professors become more aware of how systemic racism affects students from underrepresented groups. Over two years, 29 faculty members participated in these workshops designed to help them understand the challenges faced by these students better. The workshops also taught them ways they could use their positions to promote fairness and inclusivity in their teaching and mentorship roles. As a result, participants gained knowledge about how to create more inclusive environments for all students, not just those from underrepresented groups.

government.title: Exploring the Role of Internal Control Effectiveness, Information Asymmetry, and Individual Morality in Accounting Fraud: Insights from the Public Sector
government.short_title: Exploring the Role of Internal Control Effectiveness, Information Asymmetry, and Individual Mo…
government.plain_summary: Accounting fraud continues to be a significant problem affecting financial transparency, especially in the public sector. This study found that having strong internal controls and reducing information asymmetry significantly lowers the likelihood of accounting fraud. However, individual morality did not have a substantial impact on preventing fraud. Therefore, for organizations like those in the public sector, improving their internal control systems and ensuring better information transparency are crucial steps to reduce the risk of fraudulent activities.

government.title: Research on the Regulation of Anti-Unfair Competition Law on the Abuse of Trademark Rights after Malicious Registration
government.short_title: Research on the Regulation of Anti-Unfair Competition Law on the Abuse of Trademark Rights aft…
government.source: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
government.plain_summary: The Anti-Unfair Competition Law helps control misuse when someone registers a trademark maliciously. Even though there are rules against such registration, it's hard to deal with afterward because checking for malice is not strict enough. The Anti-Unfair Competition Law offers more ways to handle this issue and has broader applications. However, sometimes judges don't apply these laws correctly, leading to inconsistent rulings.

government.title: The Effect Of Good Governance And The Implementation Of Integrity Zones On Corruption Prevention (A Study On Skpd Apparatus In North Sumatra Province)
government.short_title: The Effect Of Good Governance And The Implementation Of Integrity Zones On Corruption Preventi…
government.source: Equivalent : Journal of Economic, Accounting and Management
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how good government practices and setting up special zones for integrity can help stop corruption among local government workers in North Sumatra Province. It found that when these good governance measures are put into action, there is less corruption happening. This means that by improving the way decisions are made and creating areas where people know they will be held accountable, it's easier to prevent bad behavior from officials. The research suggests that if more places follow this model, fewer corrupt actions might occur in local government.

government.title: A Critical Discourse Analysis of Philippine Media Representations of Senator Risa Hontiveros’ Anti-Political Dynasty Bill
government.short_title: A Critical Discourse Analysis of Philippine Media Representations of Senator Risa Hontiveros’…
government.source: Psychology and Education: A Multidisciplinary Journal
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how a bill to stop political dynasties is talked about in Philippine media. It uses a method called Critical Discourse Analysis to see how different groups talk about it. The bill is seen as a way to make sure everyone has an equal chance to be in power, not just those from powerful families. Supporters of the bill say it's fair and necessary for democracy.

government.title: Corrupting U?: Workplace Bullying, Ethical Erosion, and Corruption Contagion in Public Higher Education
government.short_title: Corrupting U?: Workplace Bullying, Ethical Erosion, and Corruption Contagion in Public Higher…
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how workplace bullying affects corruption in public universities. It found that when employees are bullied, they're more likely to make unethical decisions and feel less healthy at work. The research also uncovered five main ways bullying leads to corruption: unfair hiring practices, toxic environments, misuse of funds, deception, and discrimination based on race or gender. To prevent this, university leaders need to have strict rules against bullying and must encourage ethical behavior among their staff.

government.title: The Current Situation, Challenges, and Countermeasures of International Cooperation against Corruption
government.short_title: The Current Situation, Challenges, and Countermeasures of International Cooperation against Co…
government.source: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
government.plain_summary: International cooperation against corruption is crucial for tackling cross-border bribery and money laundering. China has established a framework supported by its criminal laws and treaties to facilitate extradition, repatriation, and other measures like persuasion to return. However, challenges remain such as non-extradition of death penalty cases, differences in dual crime determinations, and lack of asset sharing mechanisms. To overcome these issues, it's important to improve domestic legal systems, standardize sentencing procedures, strengthen anti-money laundering efforts, diversify cooperation routes, and enhance judicial assistance protocols.

government.title: Between nationalism and solidarity: writing on the far right, anti-gender mobilisation and LGBTQ activism in Ukraine’s war context
government.short_title: Between nationalism and solidarity: writing on the far right, anti-gender mobilisation and LGB…
government.source: European Journal of Politics and Gender
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how anti-gender groups, especially far-right nationalists in Ukraine during wartime, are perceived by both Western and Russian audiences. Historically, these groups have been seen as the main political threat to LGBTQ rights. However, in recent years, there has been a shift where some LGBTQ activists have formed alliances with nationalist groups. This complicates how researchers can study this issue ethically.

government.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE–ENABLED RECRUITMENT SYSTEMS AND TRANSPARENCY IN PUBLIC SECTOR HIRING: EVIDENCE FROM THE NATIONAL IDENTITY MANAGEMENT COMMISSION (NIMC), NIGERIA
government.short_title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE–ENABLED RECRUITMENT SYSTEMS AND TRANSPARENCY IN PUBLIC SECTOR HIRING:…
government.source: FUGUS Journal of Public Administration and Management
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how AI systems help make hiring processes more fair and clear in government jobs, focusing on Nigeria's National Identity Management Commission (NIMC). The study found that using AI makes the selection process more consistent and less influenced by personal opinions. It also creates a record of decisions that can be checked easily. This helps ensure people get jobs based on their skills rather than who they know.

government.title: ETHICS, TRANSPARENCY AND RESPONSIBLE SOURCING IN THE FEDERAL MINISTRY OF HEALTH IN NIGERIA
government.short_title: ETHICS, TRANSPARENCY AND RESPONSIBLE SOURCING IN THE FEDERAL MINISTRY OF HEALTH IN NIGERIA
government.source: FUGUS Journal of Public Administration and Management
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how ethical conduct, transparency, and responsible sourcing are practiced in Nigeria's Federal Ministry of Health. It found that while these practices can help streamline processes and improve adherence to protocols, they don't always lead to better ethics or reduce corruption. The research suggests making clear rules on ethics and providing regular training for staff and suppliers could enhance their understanding and follow them properly. This is important because it helps prevent corruption, builds trust among stakeholders, and ensures that public funds are used effectively for the benefit of everyone.

government.title: Editorial: Governance and accountability (Gover-nability) of multiple values of municipal corporations
government.short_title: Editorial: Governance and accountability (Gover-nability) of multiple values of municipal corp…
government.source: International Journal of Public Sector Management

government.title: Ethical Leadership and Public Sector Integrity:Governance Frameworks for Combating Corruption and Rebuilding Institutional Trust
government.short_title: Ethical Leadership and Public Sector Integrity:Governance Frameworks for Combating Corruption…
government.source: International Journal of Administration and Management Research Studies (IJAMRS)
government.plain_summary: This study examines how ethical leadership can improve the trust in government institutions and reduce corruption. It found that leaders who model good behavior are key to creating an honest culture within organizations. Additionally, having strong systems for handling complaints and ensuring accountability is crucial. The research suggests that simply making information public isn’t enough; what matters more is having effective investigation and enforcement capabilities.

government.title: Multi-Actor Collaboration and NGO Accountability: An NGO Case Study
government.short_title: Multi-Actor Collaboration and NGO Accountability: An NGO Case Study
government.source: Voluntas: International Journal of Voluntary and Nonprofit Organizations
government.plain_summary: This case study examines how a large NGO manages to protect its beneficiaries despite challenges from commercialization pressures. By collaborating with donors, funders, and regulators, the NGO developed new rules and norms for communication between them and beneficiaries. This helped ensure that beneficiary interests were not overlooked. However, cultural differences sometimes prevent full accountability measures being fully effective.

government.title: A Study on the Use of Blockchain Technology to Prevent and Detect Corruption in Thailand's Government Procurement Process
government.short_title: A Study on the Use of Blockchain Technology to Prevent and Detect Corruption in Thailand's Gov…
government.source: International Journal of Electronic Government Research
government.plain_summary: This research suggests using blockchain technology to help stop corruption in government buying things. It found that having a good understanding of how to use blockchain is still not common among Thai governments. The study recommends creating new systems with blockchain like smart contracts and online training programs to make sure everyone follows rules fairly during the buying process. This can improve trust between buyers, sellers, and officials.

government.title: Impact of Corruption on Public Procurement Processes in Nigeria’s Public Sector Organisations
government.short_title: Impact of Corruption on Public Procurement Processes in Nigeria’s Public Sector Organisations

government.title: Governing Algorithmic Fairness in Climate-Health Systems: A Policy Framework for Bias Mitigation in Public Sector Decision-Making
government.short_title: Governing Algorithmic Fairness in Climate-Health Systems: A Policy Framework for Bias Mitigati…
government.source: Journal of Public Policy and Local Government (JPPLG)
government.plain_summary: This article discusses how artificial intelligence is being used to help make decisions about climate and health issues in government. While this technology can be very useful, it also has the potential to unfairly treat certain groups of people if not managed properly. The paper introduces a new framework called AFCHG that helps governments use AI fairly when making these kinds of decisions. This framework includes four main parts: setting rules, ensuring fair decision-making processes, fixing any unfairness in how AI works, and considering fairness for all people.

government.title: ETHICS AND LEGAL FRAMEWORK OF PUBLIC RELATIONS VISUAL COMMUNICATION AS A MEDIA OF PUBLIC EDUCATION IN ENCOURAGING SUSTAINABLE GLOBAL ECONOMIC RECOVERY IN THE ERA OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION
government.short_title: ETHICS AND LEGAL FRAMEWORK OF PUBLIC RELATIONS VISUAL COMMUNICATION AS A MEDIA OF PUBLIC EDUCA…
government.source: International Journal of Law Government and Communication
government.plain_summary: Digital transformations have made using visuals an important part of how Public Relations communicates information. This helps educate people about things like sustainable economic recovery. But with more use of digital visuals comes new rules and ethical standards to follow. Our research looked at these issues, finding that following good ethics and staying within legal guidelines is key for effective PR communication.

government.title: Corruption in Public Procurement: From Definition towards a Case Study (Part II)
government.short_title: Corruption in Public Procurement: From Definition towards a Case Study (Part II)
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses how to prevent corruption in government buying things and services. It found that businesses often face issues like lack of transparency, dishonesty, and unfair competition when bidding on contracts. The third part looks at how one city handles these processes and suggests ways to make it easier for everyone while saving taxpayer money. By using new technology more, they could help reduce corruption and improve the process.

government.title: Who Acts, and Who is Watched? Differences Between Top-down and Bottom-up AI Anti-Corruption Tool Implementation Methods
government.short_title: Who Acts, and Who is Watched? Differences Between Top-down and Bottom-up AI Anti-Corruption To…
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how governments use artificial intelligence (AI) to fight corruption in two ways: top-down and bottom-up. Top-down methods involve government agencies using AI, which can make the process more efficient but might create a cycle where corruption is harder to detect. Bottom-up approaches let citizens participate more directly through AI tools, but they face challenges like limited access to open data. The study suggests that both methods have pros and cons, and there's a need for better integration of citizen participation with AI technology to effectively combat corruption.

government.title: Governing Money Laundering as a Collective-Action Problem: The European Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA)
government.short_title: Governing Money Laundering as a Collective-Action Problem: The European Anti-Money Laundering…
government.plain_summary: Money laundering is a significant threat affecting competitive markets, security, and consumer well-being. The European Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA) was created as part of new EU regulations to improve supervisory standards and coordinate the fight against illicit finance across Europe. AMLA combines classification functions like setting rules and standards with selective enforcement tools such as direct supervision of high-risk groups and escalation mechanisms. By viewing these aspects through a collective-action lens, it helps explain how AMLA can effectively police money laundering while also highlighting its limitations in fully addressing the issue.

government.title: Development of Anti-Corruption Declaration in Russia: Legal Aspects and Contemporary Challenges
government.short_title: Development of Anti-Corruption Declaration in Russia: Legal Aspects and Contemporary Challenges
government.plain_summary: This article looks at how Russia is making rules for people to declare if they have done anything wrong that could be seen as corrupt. In recent years, it's gotten more complicated how this works. On one hand, there are now better ways for government to check on people who might be doing bad things and use computers more. But on the other hand, fewer people can easily see these declarations because the government says they need to protect everyone from danger.

nonprofit.title: Customer Experiences with Airline Refunds: An Analysis of Procedures, Challenges, and Policy Implications
nonprofit.short_title: Customer Experiences with Airline Refunds: An Analysis of Procedures, Challenges, and Policy I…
nonprofit.source: International Journal of Research in Entrepreneurship & Business Studies
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study analyzed how airlines handle airfare refunds and the challenges customers face during this process. It found that communication issues are a major problem, especially in understanding airline rules. Despite most customers being satisfied with their refund after receiving one, they felt the process was complex and inefficient. The research suggests clearer policies and better coordination between airlines, intermediaries, and customers could improve trust and service quality.

nonprofit.title: Review of Risk Based Financial Governance Literature Shaping Institutional Investment Decision Practices
nonprofit.short_title: Review of Risk Based Financial Governance Literature Shaping Institutional Investment Decision…
nonprofit.plain_summary: Risk-based financial governance is becoming crucial for how institutions make investment decisions in today's markets. It involves assessing risks explicitly within oversight to align with organizational goals and responsibilities. This approach extends beyond traditional compliance by integrating risk into decision-making processes, using tools like scenario analysis and dynamic portfolio management. The literature shows that institutions with strong risk-based governance are better at anticipating market changes, optimizing performance, and ensuring sustainable value creation while staying compliant.

nonprofit.title: Recent Expansions in Anti-Microbial Profile of Quinoline Analogues: A Review
nonprofit.short_title: Recent Expansions in Anti-Microbial Profile of Quinoline Analogues: A Review
nonprofit.plain_summary: Recent research has shown that adding different parts called heterocyclic systems to quinoline molecules can create compounds with many useful properties. These modified quinoline-based drugs are effective against a wide range of harmful bacteria, including those causing serious infections. They also show promise in treating cancer and other conditions like seizures, pain, inflammation, and heart problems. By combining quinoline with other parts, scientists can make new medicines that work better than existing ones.

nonprofit.title: Measuring Compliance Maturity and Organizational Integrity: A Conceptual Framework for an Integrated Governance and Ethics Model
nonprofit.short_title: Measuring Compliance Maturity and Organizational Integrity: A Conceptual Framework for an Inte…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looks at how organizations measure their compliance with rules and regulations. Many existing models focus mainly on following the rules, but overlook important aspects like leadership commitment to ethics and overall organization strength. To address this, they propose an integrated model called CGMM that considers both governance (how decisions are made) and ethical practices together. This helps in better understanding how well organizations handle compliance while also ensuring strong values and integrity.

nonprofit.title: Alcohol and cancer risk: A review of messaging content on websites of medical, cancer, government, and nonprofit organizations and alcohol companies.
nonprofit.short_title: Alcohol and cancer risk: A review of messaging content on websites of medical, cancer, governm…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looked at websites from various organizations in the United States related to health, cancer, government, and nonprofits, as well as those funded by alcohol companies. Out of 126 medical society websites reviewed, about half mentioned health risks from alcohol use, with around a quarter mentioning cancer risk. Only six out of these societies stated there is no safe level of alcohol consumption. All governmental sites included both health and cancer risks related to alcohol.

nonprofit.title: Multi-Actor Collaboration and NGO Accountability: An NGO Case Study
nonprofit.short_title: Multi-Actor Collaboration and NGO Accountability: An NGO Case Study
nonprofit.source: Voluntas: International Journal of Voluntary and Nonprofit Organizations
nonprofit.plain_summary: This case study examines how a large NGO manages to protect its beneficiaries despite challenges from commercialization pressures. By collaborating with donors, funders, and regulators, the NGO developed new rules and norms for communication between them and beneficiaries. This helped ensure that beneficiary interests were not overlooked. However, cultural differences sometimes prevent full accountability measures being fully effective.

nonprofit.title: Beyond Compliance: A Systematic Review of Ethics, Accountability, And Transparency in Indonesian Governance
nonprofit.short_title: Beyond Compliance: A Systematic Review of Ethics, Accountability, And Transparency in Indonesi…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looks at how ethics, accountability, and transparency work together in Indonesian government systems. It found that even with digitalization efforts, if there isn't a strong enough foundation of ethics, these measures can fail to prevent corruption and lose public trust. The research suggests integrating ethical practices, making information transparent, and ensuring accountability are all important for effective governance. By combining these elements, Indonesia can improve its government systems and build more trustworthy relationships with the people it serves.

nonprofit.title: CHALLENGES AND DIRECTIONS FOR IMPROVING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF UKRAINE’S STATE ANTI-CORRUPTION BODIES
nonprofit.short_title: CHALLENGES AND DIRECTIONS FOR IMPROVING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF UKRAINE’S STATE ANTI-CORRUPTION B…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This article discusses key issues facing Ukraine's anti-corruption bodies and suggests ways to improve their effectiveness. Challenges include fragmented legal support, political instability, lack of coordination among agencies, limited resources, unclear jurisdictional powers, and low public trust. To address these, the Ukrainian government should focus on strengthening institutional independence, optimizing power distribution, improving human resources, enhancing coordination mechanisms, and increasing transparency in sensitive areas like procurement and financial controls. These steps are crucial for building trust with society and aligning anti-corruption efforts with European standards of governance.

nonprofit.title: Working Paper 57: Mapping and strengthening the evidence base for anti-corruption Collective Action
nonprofit.short_title: Working Paper 57: Mapping and strengthening the evidence base for anti-corruption Collective A…
nonprofit.source: Basel Institute on Governance Working Papers
nonprofit.plain_summary: This working paper offers a new way to understand how different groups like businesses, non-profits, and governments can work together more effectively against corruption. It includes tools that help researchers, practitioners, and policymakers compare various anti-corruption efforts and see what works best in different places. By understanding how these collaborations impact real-world changes in preventing corruption, it helps design better partnerships to make a difference. This paper is supported by Siemens and comes from the Basel Institute on Governance.
